title: Apartamente de vânzare în Sector 3: între anunț și act stau 94 de euro pe metru
seoTitle: Apartments for Sale Sector 3: Asking vs Paid Price
description: In Sector 3, asking prices are 1,771 euros per square meter, transactions close at 1,677, and apartments sell in 102 days. Verified figures.
descriptionLlm: Cauti apartamente in Sectorul 3? Afla pretul mediu de 1.925 euro/mp si cum variare costurile intre zona Titan si Pallady in 2026.
keywords: apartamente sector 3 de vanzare, apartamente de vanzare sector 3 bucuresti, pret apartamente sector 3, pret metru patrat sector 3, bloc nou sector 3 titan, tranzactii imobiliare sector 3
lead: In Sector 3, listings ask for 1,771 euros per square meter. Notary deeds from August 2026 show 1,677 euros. The figures come from different measurements, one from listings and the other from transactions, and placed side by side they reveal a simple fact: sellers ask for 94 euros more per square meter than what buyers actually pay. We analyzed the numbers one by one, along with how long an apartment stays on the market and the price of new buildings, so you know exactly what money is being discussed. The difference between 1,771 and 1,677 is not just statistical dust, as it amounts to 5,640 euros for a 60 square meter two-room apartment. Moreover, the market is moving, with Sonarhome estimating transactions reaching 1,811 euros per square meter for September.

sections.h2: They Ask for 1,771 Euros per Meter and It Sells for 1,677

blocks.x: The first figure comes from listings. Pretimobil measures active listings in the sector, and today, September 15, 2026, the average asking price is 1,771 euros per square meter. The second figure comes from official deeds, with Sonarhome calculating it from actual transactions at 1,677 euros per square meter for August 2026, alongside an estimate of 1,811 for the current month.

Here is what the figure from the deed looks like for a specific apartment: in March 2026, a 43 square meter two-room apartment on the ground floor of a building built in 1976 on Patriotilor Street 2 sold for 86,000 euros. This comes out to 2,000 euros per square meter, which is above the sector average because for smaller surfaces, base costs are divided among fewer meters.

sections.h2: For a Two-Room Apartment, the Difference Equals 5,640 Euros

blocks.x: Subtract 1,677 from 1,771 and you get 94 euros per square meter. For a 60 square meter two-room apartment, which is common in the sector, the difference reaches 5,640 euros. With this money, you can cover more than twice the reservation fee requested for a new building in the area, where discussions start at 2,000 euros plus VAT.

The figure from the deeds works both ways. The buyer has it on their side because the seller sets the price based on listings, while August transactions show where a serious discussion ends. The seller, in turn, learns from this same difference why an overpriced listing sits for months without a signature.

sections.h2: An Apartment in Sector 3 Takes About Three Months and a Half to Sell

blocks.x: Sonarhome also measures time: from listing to signature, an average of 102 days pass. This equals 3.4 months, a quarter of a year during which the apartment receives visits and counteroffers. Meanwhile, the supply is shrinking, with 11.72 percent fewer listings available in the sector compared to the previous month.

The numbers fit together: fewer apartments on the market and the estimate of 1,811 euros per square meter for September point to a sector where price drops are unlikely. For buyers, those 102 days become an advantage, as a seller who has already waited three months is much more willing to listen to a serious offer.

sections.h2: Titan Asks 2,100 Euros per Meter, While Mihai Bravu Settles for 1,750

blocks.x: Within the sector, neighborhoods have different price expectations. Listings from August 25, 2026, showed an asking price of 2,100 euros per square meter in Titan, Dristor stood at 1,950 euros, Pallady dropped to 1,850 euros, and Mihai Bravu reached 1,750 euros. Even at the cheapest end of the sector, with 1,750 requested, the price remains above the transaction average of 1,677, meaning the gap between asking and closing prices does not disappear anywhere in Sector 3. You can track current listings at apartamentele de vânzare, while deed figures remain the benchmark for comparison.

sections.h2: New Buildings Demand Different Budgets Than Older Sector Panels

blocks.x: The Imobiliare.ro index shows 2,549 euros per square meter for new apartments in Bucharest and 2,265 for older ones in August 2026. The difference between the city average for new blocks and the second-hand market in the sector for 60 square meters reaches 52,320 euros. We are talking about averages, not two specific apartments, but this difference explains why older panels easily find buyers and why new buildings require a completely different budget category.

A concrete example comes from Titan: a new building on Eprubetei Alley 7-11, a five-minute walk from Nicolae Grigorescu subway station and nine minutes from IOR Park, asks between 107,500 and 136,500 euros for two rooms, plus 21 percent VAT, which applies starting August 1, 2025, through Law 141/2025. With VAT included, the range climbs between 130,075 and 165,165 euros. Three-room apartments start at 151,000 and go up to 168,000 euros plus VAT, meaning between 182,710 and 203,280 euros payable.

Here, the listing price is the payment price: the developer sells directly with no buyer commission, and the price includes underfloor heating, Salamander seven-chamber tri-pane windows, a 24 kW Ariston boiler, and a short floor plan with only four apartments per level. Parking is paid separately, at 20,000 euros plus VAT for a single space and 25,000 euros plus VAT for a double Klauss system.

The minimum down payment is 30 percent of the price without VAT, reaching 32,250 euros for the most affordable two-room apartment, after the 2,000 euros plus VAT reservation fee. The rest usually comes from a mortgage, and in the ghidul de credit ipotecar you can calculate your down payment and monthly installment before signing. The building is scheduled for delivery in December 2026, so you sign before seeing it finished; today, on September 17, 2026, out of 35 apartments, only 6 are left available.

sections.h2: Sector 3 Ranks Third in the City and Below Listing Averages

blocks.x: Sonarhome places Sector 3 in third place among Bucharest sectors by price. City figures, each calculated in its own way, look like this: the Imobiliare.ro index shows an average of 2,304 euros per square meter in August 2026, up 9.4 percent from August 2025, while the listing average measured by hartapreturilor across 295 active listings in September 2026 is 1,856 euros per square meter. These three measurements do not merge into a single number because each comes from a different sample; you should read them as layers of the same market. You can view the rest of the areas side by side in prețurile apartamentelor.

The sector sits below the city listing average with 1,771 requested and drops even lower with 1,677 paid. For anyone comparing neighborhoods, this is the short story of the sector: mid-range pricing in the city rankings and a 94 euro per square meter gap between the storefront and reality.

faq.q: How much is actually paid per square meter in Sector 3?
faq.a: 1,677 euros per square meter, according to notary deeds from August 2026. The asking price was 1,771, meaning sellers ask for 94 euros more per square meter than the final transaction amount.

faq.q: Is it worth waiting for a price drop if you want an apartment in Sector 3?
faq.a: Data measured today does not point toward a price drop. Available listings in the sector decreased by 11.72 percent in a month, Sonarhome estimates transactions reaching 1,811 euros per square meter for September, and the Imobiliare.ro index rose by 9.4 percent compared to August 2025. However, you can work with time: an apartment stays on the market for an average of 102 days, and a seller who has already lost three months will seriously listen to an offer with ready funds. Therefore, having money ready and targeting an apartment that has been sitting for months will get you further than pure patience.

faq.q: How much does a new apartment cost in Sector 3?
faq.a: A reference example from Titan, the building on Eprubetei Alley: two rooms cost between 107,500 and 136,500 euros plus 21 percent VAT, meaning between 130,075 and 165,165 euros with VAT included. Three-room apartments start at 182,710 and reach 203,280 euros payable. To these, you add the 2,000 euros plus VAT reservation and a minimum down payment of 30 percent of the price without VAT, with the building scheduled for delivery in December 2026.
